title: Weekly Agenda
description: Solo consultants and small teams: tasks and meetings by day, with a Friday review.

spec.useCase: Celeste Abernathy-Voss runs a small advisory practice and uses this to lay out each week by day, with tasks and meetings together, and review it on Friday.

business.name: Windrose Advisory
business.describes: A small advisory firm helping farm co-ops plan and fund their next stage.

text.text: A work week, day by day. Plan the week in one glance. Each day lists its tasks and meetings. Add the week’s single focus first, then fill the days.
Twenty minutes. Look back before you look ahead.
Move anything unfinished to a day next week or drop it
Write two lines on how the week went in the Weeks table
Note one thing to do differently
Clear your desk and your inbox
Pick the one focus that would make the week a success.
Put meetings on their days first; they are fixed.
Place the focus work in the longest gaps.
Fill gaps with small tasks, never more than six hours a day.
When everything is important, nothing finishes. One focus makes tradeoffs easy to see.
Move tasks to another day by editing the Day. Do not rewrite the plan; adjust it.
